subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw extend the official status/usage JSON contracts with stable per-session attribution fields, and what privacy policy should apply to cron and channel identifiers?
rationale: The request is valid but changes an official JSON/API surface and asks for potentially sensitive channel/cron attribution fields, so automation should not choose the permanent field names or identifier policy alone.

options.title: Add narrow attribution fields
options.body: Add stable non-sensitive fields such as `agentId`, `sessionKind`, `cronJobId` or redacted name, `channel`, `channelTargetKind`, model, and runtime with docs and regression tests, omitting raw target ids by default.

options.title: Limit to current usage APIs
options.body: Keep existing `sessions.usage` and status JSON shapes unchanged and document how external dashboards can join with session/cron metadata themselves.

options.title: Defer to telemetry export design
options.body: Leave this issue open as input for a broader telemetry/export contract instead of changing status JSON directly.

recommendation.title: Add narrow attribution fields
recommendation.body: Add stable non-sensitive fields such as `agentId`, `sessionKind`, `cronJobId` or redacted name, `channel`, `channelTargetKind`, model, and runtime with docs and regression tests, omitting raw target ids by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged usage-RPC work and review history make this the strongest available owner for the API/product shape decision.
